title: Agentic AI for Autonomous Defense in Software Supply Chain Security: Beyond Provenance to Vulnerability Mitigation
review_status: full-text audit; reported results not independently auditable from paper detail
evidence_note: Reports simulated and GitHub Actions/Jenkins evaluation across four vulnerability classes, >90% autonomous mitigation and <6% overhead, but reviewed text gives no named repository/sample inventory, denominators, splits, uncertainty or linked code/data; figures are plots without numeric tables. This limits independent auditability, not proof of falsity.

title: Evaluating the Generalizability of LLMs in Automated Program Repair
sections_checked: §III transformed Defects4J construction and model/prompt setup
Tables II–III: 11-model generalization and four-model repair-context results
§V threats to validity and §VI future work
evidence_note: Across 11 open models, mean correct/plausible fixes fell 49.48%/42.90% on transformed Defects4J; repair context improved four selected weak generalizers, but 10/12 tested setups remained below original-set performance. Same 438 single-function Java bugs transformed; manual semantic patch review and model/language coverage are limits.

title: SoK: Agentic Skills -- Beyond Tool Use in LLM Agents
evidence_note: Survey/map rather than independent efficacy experiment; taxonomy is a synthesis not externally validated. Its cited skill benchmark snapshot is superseded by current SkillsBench v4, so current empirical claims were verified against primary benchmark and follow-up papers.

title: SkillsBench: Benchmarking How Well Agent Skills Work Across Diverse Tasks
review_status: citation follow-up; current primary benchmark version audited
sections_checked: task-level negative deltas and trajectory audit
Appendix ecosystem quality and benchmark/ecosystem limitation
evidence_note: Across 87 tasks and 18 configurations, 3 trials/cell, curated Skills increase macro pass rate 33.9% to 50.5% (+16.6 pp), with configuration gains +4.1 to +25.7 pp; 13/87 tasks have negative deltas. Selected benchmark Skills are top-quality-quartile; authors state benchmark is optimistic versus ecosystem.

title: SkillAxe: Sharpening LLM-Authored Agent Skills Through Evaluation-Guided Self-Refinement
review_status: citation follow-up; independent mechanism and transfer evidence audited
evidence_note: Different/older SkillsBench snapshot, single Claude Opus 4.5+Harbor setup and k=2. Native score improvement 26.7% to 41.6% comes entirely from evaluable-output coverage (conditional native quality remains 57.1%); on SpreadsheetBench held-out N=50, SkillAxe and LLM-self libraries both score 52%. LLM judging and cross-version/protocol noncomparability limit direct comparison.

title: A Metamorphic Testing Approach to Diagnosing Memorization in LLM-Based Program Repair
review_status: citation follow-up; independent cross-paper counterevidence and protocol audited
evidence_note: Seven models show significant transformed Defects4J drops (4.01–15.98 points) among originally solvable bugs; newer GitBug-Java has no significant average decline for GPT-4o/Claude-3.7, and GPT-4o-mini p=.074, but individual large regressions remain. Small solvable sample limits power; NLL is a familiarity proxy, not proof of leakage.

title: End-to-End Optimization of LLM-Driven Multi-Agent Search Systems via Heterogeneous-Group-Based Reinforcement Learning
evidence_note: MHGPO improves retrieval QA in HotpotQA/2Wiki/MuSiQue for a three-agent pipeline with up-to-8B backbone; e.g. HotpotQA F1 21.45 unoptimized MAS to 50.86 one variant. Authors explicitly limit evaluation to static multi-hop QA, fixed 3 agents, up to 8B; no direct evidence for open-ended research agents.
